title: Count Distinct Palindromic Substrings
statement:
Given a string `s` consisting of lowercase English letters, determine how many **distinct** substrings of `s` are palindromes.

A substring is a contiguous block of characters. A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. Two substrings are the same if they consist of the same characters in the same order, no matter where they occur in `s`, and each distinct palindrome is counted once.

For example, in `aabaa` the distinct palindromic substrings are `a`, `b`, `aa`, `aba` and `aabaa`, so the answer is 5.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of distinct palindromic substrings of `s`.
constraints: s consists of lowercase letters a-z

examples.explanation: The distinct palindromic substrings are a, b, aa, aba and aabaa. The second `a` and the second `aa` are repeats and are not counted again.
Only the single letters a, b and c are palindromes.
The substrings a, aa, aaa and aaaa are palindromes; every other substring is a repeat of one of them.

hints: Counting all palindromic substrings is easy with expand-around-center. The difficulty is not counting the same palindrome twice.
A string of length n has at most n distinct palindromic substrings. Whenever you append a character, at most one new palindrome appears, and it must be a suffix of the new string.

Maintain a palindromic tree (eertree): each node is a distinct palindrome, edges add the same letter on both sides, and each node keeps a suffix link to its longest proper palindromic suffix. The answer is the number of nodes created (a hashing approach over all O(n^2) palindromes also works at this size, but is much heavier).
